the heme-pocket relaxation dynamics of (carbon monoxy)hemoglobin are solvent viscosity dependent, while the prompt ligand-rebinding kinetics and the heme-pocket geometry that are established within 10-100 ns of photolysis are not.

solvent viscosity strongly influences the relaxation dynamics of photolytic heme-pocket geometry but does not significantly affect the rate of ligand recombination or the initial heme-pocket geometry.

solvent viscosity affects the heme pocket relaxation process, which is a consequence of protein dynamics.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relaxation of the proximal ligand-binding pocket of hemoglobin is not a local event but a global one, and it is this relaxation that determines the ligand recombination dynamics.
the relaxation of the heme pocket is a two-step process, with a fast, local, and solvent-independent relaxation followed by a slow, global, and solvent-dependent relaxation.

the heme-pocket relaxation dynamics are more sensitive to solvent viscosity than the geminate recombination process.
the relaxation dynamics of heme-pocket geometry in hemoglobin are not governed by a single, simple mechanism.
